Turn 1 of 4 — read-back. Do not write any program JSON in this turn.

You are going to turn a protocol into a Rhylthyme program: parallel **tracks** of sequential **steps**, each with a duration and a start trigger, that one person follows against a live clock.

Plan this as a Rhylthyme protocol and deliver a live timeline: Passaging Two Flasks of Adherent HEK293 Cells for two T75 flasks split 1:6 into four
Resource limits: one biosafety cabinet, one 37 °C water bath, one CO₂ incubator, one benchtop centrifuge, one microscope with haemocytometer, one operator.
No finishing time was given; finish as early as the work allows.

Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Passaging Two Flasks of Adherent HEK293 Cells

Two T75 flasks at about 90 % confluence are split 1:6 into four new flasks. The room has one biosafety cabinet, one 37 °C water bath, one CO₂ incubator, one benchtop centrifuge and one microscope with a haemocytometer. Only one flask can be open in the cabinet at a time, so the two flasks queue for it while the centrifuge and the microscope stay free. Work with pre-warmed medium, PBS and trypsin-EDTA throughout; nothing cold touches the cells. One operator.

Preparation
1. Wipe down the cabinet, lay out pipettes and tubes, and let the blower run; 10 minutes.
2. Check both flasks on the microscope for confluence and contamination; 10 minutes.

Flask A
3. Aspirate the spent medium and rinse the monolayer with 5 mL of PBS; 4 minutes in the cabinet.
4. Add 2 mL of trypsin-EDTA, rock the flask and return it to the incubator for 5 minutes.
5. Knock the flask, check detachment and neutralise with 8 mL of medium; 5 minutes in the cabinet.
6. Transfer the suspension to a 15 mL tube and spin at 300 × g for 5 minutes.
7. Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 10 mL of fresh medium; 4 minutes.
8. Count the cells on the haemocytometer; 6 minutes.
9. Seed two new T75 flasks at 1:6 and label them; 6 minutes in the cabinet.
10. Return the new flasks to the incubator and leave them to settle overnight, at least 16 hours.

Flask B
11. Start flask B the moment flask A leaves the cabinet: aspirate and rinse with 5 mL of PBS; 4 minutes.
12. Trypsinise flask B in the incubator for 5 minutes.
13. Neutralise flask B as soon as flask A is out of the cabinet again; 5 minutes.
14. Spin flask B at 300 × g for 5 minutes once the centrifuge is free.
15. Resuspend the flask B pellet in 10 mL of fresh medium; 4 minutes.
16. Count flask B on the haemocytometer once flask A has been counted; 6 minutes.
17. Seed two more T75 flasks at 1:6 and label them; 6 minutes.
18. Return them to the incubator to settle overnight alongside the first pair.

Finishing
19. Wipe the cabinet down, discard the waste and switch the blower to standby; 10 minutes.
20. Write the passage number, the split ratio and the counts into the culture log; 5 minutes.
>>>

Read all of it before you answer. Then say back, in one paragraph and in your own words: what is being made, for how many (or at what scale), by when, and under what constraints — equipment that exists only once, how many people are working, anything that has to be held, rested or ready at a particular moment. If the text you were given looks truncated, or points at a section that is not here, say so instead of filling the gap.

End your reply with the same read-back as JSON in a single ```json fenced block:

```json
  "servesOrScale": "8 people",
  "deadline": "2026-11-26T18:00:00",
  "constraints": ["one oven", "two burners", "two cooks"]
}
```

**Read-back.** This run passages two adherent HEK293 T75 flasks sitting at roughly 90 % confluence, splitting them 1:6 into four fresh T75 flasks — the text has each parent flask (A, then B) seeding two new flasks — so the output is four new T75 flasks that are then left to settle overnight. There is no clock time and no finishing time anywhere in the text, only the instruction that the hands-on work finishes as early as it can; the one fixed horizon is biological rather than diarised, the post-seeding overnight settle of at least 16 hours, which is the true tail of the protocol and the thing that ends the run. Everything is done by a single operator, so the person is a capacity-1 resource in their own right and the two flasks can never be worked in parallel — they interleave. Five instruments exist exactly once: one biosafety cabinet, one 37 °C water bath, one CO₂ incubator, one benchtop centrifuge, one microscope with haemocytometer; the cabinet is the binding one because only one flask may be open in it at a time, which is why flask B starts the instant flask A leaves the cabinet (step 11) and is neutralised as soon as A is out again (step 13), while the centrifuge and microscope are explicitly free by the time each flask needs them — A spins before B needs it, A is counted before B is counted. The incubator does double duty: it gives each flask its 5-minute trypsin-EDTA incubation and later receives all four new flasks for the overnight settle. Nothing cold may touch the cells — medium, PBS and trypsin-EDTA are pre-warmed throughout — so the water bath is a genuine prerequisite step for the reagents, not decoration. The text looks complete: all four sections (Preparation, Flask A, Flask B, Finishing) and steps 1–20 are present, nothing points at a section that is missing. One thing I've taken as written rather than reconciled: a 1:6 split would normally give six daughters per parent, yet the steps describe seeding two new flasks per parent, so I've treated 1:6 as the stated dilution ratio and the four-flask yield as the stated scale.

**Model check — restated in my own words.**

A **track** is one sequential line of work — a single station, instrument or person doing one thing after another — and because steps inside a track never overlap, anything that must happen *while* something else is happening has to live in a different track so the runner can run the two lines in parallel. A **step** is one piece of work and carries exactly one duration kind: `fixed` with `seconds` (e.g. the 5-minute trypsin incubation), `variable` with `minSeconds`/`maxSeconds`/`defaultSeconds` (e.g. a check whose length depends on what you see), or `indefinite`, which runs until the person ends it and just wants a `defaultSeconds` so previews look sane. A **startTrigger** is what ties a step to the clock or to another step: `programStart` at t=0, `programStartOffset` at a fixed offset, `afterStep` (optionally with an `offsetSeconds`, an `event: "start"`, a `choiceId`, or an `instances` mode) when another step ends, `afterStepWithBuffer` for a gap, `manual` for a tap-to-start, `onAbort` for cleanup-only paths, and `compound` to wait for all or the first of several triggers — with `afterStep` references having to point at real steps and never form a cycle. `stepId`s are unique across the WHOLE program, not per track, so I must not reuse `aspirate` in both the Flask A and Flask B lines. Every `task` a step occupies needs a matching `resourceConstraints` entry, and that entry's `maxConcurrent` is the real enforcement — it is what stops two steps sharing one cabinet, one water bath or one incubator, independently of how I sequence the tracks. Work repeated n times is `replicates: {count: n, mode: "serial" | "parallel" | "stagger"}` on ONE step rather than n hand-copied steps; whatever follows each repetition chains with `{"type":"afterStep","stepId":"<step>","instances":"each"}`, the step that waits for all of them gets `{"instances":"all"}`, and if the holding area between repetitions only fits k at a time, `replicates.maxInFlight: k` holds the upstream work back instead of stranding the downstream work.

For this protocol the resource list is small, honest and almost entirely `maxConcurrent: 1`, because the text gives one of each instrument and one operator. The **cabinet** is the binding singleton (only one flask open at a time, so Flask A and Flask B's cabinet steps form one serialising chain); the **bath** is claimed by the pre-warming of medium/PBS/trypsin ("nothing cold touches the cells"); the **incubator** is claimed twice over — the per-flask 5-minute trypsinisation and then the four new flasks' overnight settle; the **centrifuge** and the **microscope** (one unit, haemocytometer included) are each `maxConcurrent: 1` and stay free by stagger rather than by queueing. I'll also give the bench work its own **prep** task at `maxConcurrent: 1` for out-of-cabinet handling — labelling, resuspension, the culture log — since it happens at a different place from the cabinet even though the same person does it. People are represented as `actors: 1`, a single operator, so no two steps can be hands-on at the same instant; the only deliberate *holding* in the model is the ≥16 h overnight settle, which I'll model as the final long step rather than an instrument wait.

```json
{
  "acknowledgement": "tracks are sequential lines of work with no overlap inside a track, so anything concurrent goes in its own track; each step has exactly one duration kind (fixed/variable/indefinite); a startTrigger ties a step to the clock (programStart, programStartOffset, manual) or to another step (afterStep, afterStepWithBuffer, onAbort, compound); stepIds are unique across the whole program, not per track; every task a step occupies needs a matching resourceConstraints entry whose maxConcurrent is what actually stops two steps sharing one instrument; repeated work is replicates on one step, chained onward with instances each, joined with instances all, and held back with maxInFlight where the holding area is the limit",
  "resourceConstraints": [
    { "task": "cabinet", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "bath", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "incubator", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "centrifuge", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "microscope", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "prep", "maxConcurrent": 1 }
  ],
  "actors": 1
}
```

**Extraction.** Twenty numbered activities, but three of them bundle parts that occupy different resources, and one resource — the water bath — is implied by the text without ever being scheduled. So I split and add as follows.

*Splits (different resource, different stretch of time):* "**Add 2 mL of trypsin-EDTA, rock the flask** and **return it to the incubator for 5 minutes**" is cabinet time plus incubator time, so that becomes two activities (step 4, and again for flask B at step 12). "**Transfer the suspension to a 15 mL tube** and **spin at 300 × g for 5 minutes**" is bench time plus centrifuge time, so that becomes two (step 6). Nothing else in the text mixes resources: steps 1 and 19 are all cabinet, step 5 is all cabinet, step 3 and 11 are all cabinet, step 2 is all microscope.

*Inferred (few and obvious):* (a) **pre-warm the medium, PBS and trypsin-EDTA in the 37 °C water bath** — the text says "work with pre-warmed medium, PBS and trypsin-EDTA throughout; nothing cold touches the cells", which cannot happen without a warming step, and it is the only activity that would ever occupy the bath; (b) a **transfer of flask B's suspension to a 15 mL tube** before step 14 spins it — the text spells this out for flask A at step 6 but only says "spin flask B" at step 14, and a suspension has to be in a tube to be spun. That is the whole inferred list; I have deliberately *not* invented equilibration, thawing or extra checks.

*Notes on durations:* eight activities carry an explicit time in the text and I've taken those verbatim; the two short handling activities I had to split out are given as ranges since the text never times them; the overnight settle is the ≥16 h tail and appears twice in the text (once per pair of new flasks), sitting in the same incubator.

*Not decided here, as instructed:* triggers, tracks and overlaps. But two extraction facts will shape the next turn — the trypsinisation (incubator) and the settle (incubator) are the same single incubator, and step 11, step 13, step 14 and step 16 all contain an explicit hand-off from flask A ("the moment flask A leaves the cabinet", "as soon as flask A is out of the cabinet again", "once the centrifuge is free", "once flask A has been counted").
